incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the FBI's recruitment site via an Oracle PeopleSoft platform managed by an Accenture contractor who failed to apply a security patch; credentials/access abuse followed.
incidents.impact: Exposed medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers, home addresses, and unit/specialization details for thousands of FBI employees. Accenture contractor removed from the account; FBI has arrested multiple suspected ShinyHunters associates, including a ransomware negotiator (Edward Dubrovsky) suspected of helping run the extortion site.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; company confirmed suspicious IT activity detected the prior week was caused by malicious actors and filed a police report in the Netherlands.
incidents.impact: Online ordering and e-commerce systems taken offline across US and European brands; stores remained open. No confirmed data theft yet; investigation ongoing. Company previously had 2.2 million customers' data stolen in a 2024 breach.

incidents.vector: Threat actor obtained credentials tied to ConnectWise's Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application and used them to authenticate into customers' Microsoft 365 tenants, abusing highly elevated permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All.
incidents.impact: ConnectWise disabled Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services; backups and restores unavailable for partners/clients. No confirmed data exfiltration yet; full blast radius across downstream MSP customers still under investigation.

incidents.vector: Ad-tech company Discover-Tech used targeted ad-bidding infrastructure (dubbed "AdFection") to deliver Candiru spyware via ad impressions, requiring no click from the victim.
incidents.impact: At least 45 devices belonging to Al-Jazeera personnel infected with surveillance spyware. Candiru (now Integrity Labs) remains on the US Commerce Department's Entity List for supplying spyware to foreign governments.

incidents.victim: Serbian opposition and civil society figures
incidents.attacker: Unknown — government surveillance using commercial spyware (Pegasus)
incidents.vector: NSO Group's Pegasus spyware deployed against the phones of regime critics, including a university rector and a prosecutor, ahead of national elections.
incidents.impact: University of Belgrade rector Vladan Đokić confirmed infected with Pegasus; prosecutor Rade Bajić received an Apple threat notification. At least 15 Serbian civil-society figures targeted with spyware in 2026, days before the October 25 elections.
Customer data stolen from major Russian hosting provider FirstVDS.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud and identity theft
incidents.vector: Spearphishing emails used to gain access to tax preparation businesses' electronic systems beginning in 2019.
incidents.impact: Tax and identifying information stolen for at least 800 customers per compromised business across multiple US tax firms. Nigerian national Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu sentenced to eight years in prison for his role in the scheme.

incidents.vector: Threat actor tracked as TAG-217 used ARTEX, a Chinese-language open-source AI penetration-testing framework, to compromise different systems at each target, with infrastructure staging dating back to August 2026.
incidents.impact: Personal data of at least 68,000 people exposed across at least seven financial institutions; one breach exposed an outsourced developer's access, another resulted in customer data theft. Further prep infrastructure for crypto-wallet theft and mobile exploitation uncovered.

incidents.vector: Compromised versions of the OVHcloud command line tool package shipped an infostealer for a few hours before being pulled.
incidents.impact: Users who installed the compromised package were exposed to credential-stealing malware. Fixed in version 0.16.0; OVHcloud recommends pinning package hashes.

incidents.vector: Campaign (tracked as CL-UNK-1211) used AI-generated payloads, open-source tools, custom cross-platform backdoors, and web shells to target Linux environments, active from October 2025 to April 2026.
incidents.impact: Attackers conducted extensive reconnaissance, dumped sensitive databases, exfiltrated government mailboxes, and attempted to access social media accounts; used anti-forensic techniques including log wiping and planting fake red-team markers.

incidents.vector: Attackers (tracked as CL-STA-0954/UNC5820) exploited CVE-2024-47575 against a FortiManager appliance in September 2024, then exploited CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident, network-traffic-based implant leaving no file artifacts.
incidents.impact: Exfiltrated configuration, cryptographic material, and database files for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls protecting the target's own infrastructure and its clients' networks; long-term access, traffic interception, and backdoors established.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — state-linked espionage group (Kazakhstan-linked, medium confidence)
incidents.vector: UAT-6275 used macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub-hosted PowerShell, and a WinRAR exploit (CVE-2025-8088) to deploy custom reverse shells, active from June 2025 through August 2026.
incidents.impact: Targeted government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States, with additional interest in water and energy sectors; researchers gained visibility into the group's tooling and C2 infrastructure via exposed staging servers.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure and global organizations (government, healthcare, IT, manufacturing)
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group (enabled by Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: Combined automated scanning tools, botnets, and hands-on exploitation including XSS and password spraying against Microsoft Exchange servers, with persistence via VPN software.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data and credentials exfiltrated from organizations worldwide, including US critical infrastructure sectors; joint CISA/NSA/NCSC advisory issued with indicators of compromise.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized third-party access to the servers hosting the MrMax app and online store, detected October 3.
incidents.impact: Member IDs, names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, and birthdates exposed for up to 1,735,154 members; credit card data, passwords, and purchase history were not affected.

incidents.vector: Attackers (tracked as CL-STA-1178) impersonated Dubai Airports' IT department to deliver trojanized coding challenges, using legitimate Windows developer files, AppDomainManager hijacking, and DLL sideloading to deploy custom malware (ShelbyLoader V2), with GitHub infrastructure misused for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Campaign ("Blinder Tunnel") targeted Iraqi critical infrastructure in March 2026 following infrastructure staging as early as November 2025; GitHub has taken down the identified malicious infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized push notification sent to customers; attacker accessed personal information in the process.
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed; company does not believe payment card data or account passwords were affected. Investigation ongoing.
